teaser.en: Coffee with ginger after an operation: on the coast this spicy root is trusted to help people back on their feet.

summary.en: *Tangawizi* is ginger, a spicy root used in tea, coffee, cooking and medicine. Some is grown in gardens, but most is bought.

about.en: Ginger is a leafy plant with tall, reed-like stems carrying narrow, pointed leaves in two rows. The part used is the rhizome, an underground stem that is knobbly and pale brown outside, with a fibrous, pale yellow, hot and fragrant flesh.

where.en: Ginger is grown in some gardens on the south coast, but most is bought.

uses.en: Ginger goes into tea, as *chai ya tangawizi*, and into the strong black coffee of the coast. It is used in cooking and in medicine.

culture.en: Ginger coffee is thought of as a restorative; in Digo, coffee with ginger is the drink recommended after an operation.

names.en: The Digo name is *tangawizi*, the same as in Swahili. In English it is ginger.

reason.en: Another kitchen spice used in medicine

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
